title: eludite.debug.toggle_breakpoint input
description: Debug > Toggle Breakpoint (F9, or a click in the editor's breakpoint margin), and the Breakpoints window's edits: set, change or delete the breakpoint on a line, a tracepoint (`log_message`: Visual Studio's "When Hit... Print a message and Continue") or a function breakpoint (`function`). Breakpoints persist per solution and apply to a running session at once. Conditions are C# expressions evaluated by the debugger; a hit condition breaks only on some hits. A `log_message` with `{expression}` segments runs debuggee code at every hit (as a condition does), so such a call is of the execute class.
x-eludite-escalates: Only a tracepoint whose `log_message` has an `{expression}` (it runs debuggee code at every hit): dangerous when the solution's policy sets `debug.drive` or `debug.evaluate` to `prompt`, refused for agents when either is `deny`. Plain breakpoints keep the declared class.

path.description: The source file (absolute or relative to the solution folder). Default: the active document. Not with `function`.

line.description: 1-based line. Default: the caret's line in the active document. Not with `function`.

action.description: `toggle` (default): add a breakpoint, or delete the one on the line. `set`: add or change it with the fields given. `delete`: delete it. `delete_all`: delete every breakpoint, function breakpoints included (path and line are ignored). With `function`, `set` or `delete` only.

enabled.description: With `set`: enable or disable the breakpoint (it stays in the Breakpoints window).

condition.description: With `set`: break only when this expression is true. An empty string removes the condition.

hit_condition.description: With `set`: break only when the hit count is `N` (equal to N), `>=N` (at least N) or `%N` (a multiple of N), as Visual Studio's Hit Count. An empty string removes it.

log_message.description: With `set`: make it a tracepoint. At every hit the message is written to the Output window's Debug source and to the `debug` output (eludite.debug.output) and the debuggee continues without a visible stop. `{expression}` segments are evaluated in the hit frame (an evaluation error is written in place as `{expression: <error>}`; `{{` and `}}` are literal braces); `$FUNCTION` (the method), `$CALLER` (its caller), `$TID` (the thread id) and `$TNAME` (the thread name) are replaced, other `$` words are left as text. Where the debug adapter has no log points (netcoredbg) the debugger stops, writes the line and resumes at once (a stop and a resume per hit); a message with a `$` special is always written that way. An empty string turns the tracepoint back into a breakpoint. Not with `function`.

function.description: A function breakpoint by name, `Namespace.Type.Method` (DAP setFunctionBreakpoints), with `action` `set` (with `enabled`, `condition`, `hit_condition` as a source breakpoint) or `delete`. It has no path or line; the Breakpoints window names it by the function. Refused while a session runs on a debug adapter without function breakpoints (`capabilities.function_breakpoints` in eludite.debug.state).

remove_after.description: With `set`: delete the breakpoint at its first visible stop ("Delete breakpoint when hit"; eludite.debug.run_until's points do this). Default false.
